Let
\[
S=X_1+\cdots+X_N,\qquad T=N-S
\]
be the number of failures. Since the vector is exchangeable, the law is determined by the distribution of \(T\).

We have
\[
\mathbb E[T]=N(1-p),
\]
and
\[
\mathbb E[T(T-1)]
= N(N-1)\Big((1-p)^2+\rho p(1-p)\Big).
\]
Thus
\[
\frac{\mathbb E[T(T-1)]}{\mathbb E[T]}
=(N-1)(1-p+\rho p).
\]

Put
\[
A=(N-1)p(1-\rho),\qquad r=\lfloor A\rfloor,\qquad h=A-r.
\]
Then \(0\le h<1\), and
\[
(N-1)(1-p+\rho p)=N-1-A.
\]

Now size-bias the positive values of \(T\): define a probability distribution \(W\) on \(\{1,\dots,N\}\) by
\[
\mathbb P(W=t)=\frac{t\mathbb P(T=t)}{\mathbb E[T]}.
\]
Then
\[
\mathbb E[W-1]=N-1-A,
\]
so
\[
\mathbb E[W]=N-A=N-r-h.
\]
This lies between
\[
N-r-1 \quad\text{and}\quad N-r.
\]

Also
\[
\mathbb P(T>0)
=\sum_{t=1}^N \mathbb P(T=t)
=\mathbb E[T]\mathbb E\!\left[\frac1W\right].
\]
Therefore maximizing \(\mathbb P(T=0)\) is the same as minimizing
\[
\mathbb E\!\left[\frac1W\right]
\]
among distributions on \(\{1,\dots,N\}\) with mean \(N-r-h\).

Since \(t\mapsto 1/t\) is convex, the minimum occurs by placing \(W\) only on the two adjacent integers \(N-r-1\) and \(N-r\). The weights must be
\[
\mathbb P(W=N-r-1)=h,\qquad
\mathbb P(W=N-r)=1-h.
\]
Hence
\[
\min \mathbb E\!\left[\frac1W\right]
=
\frac{h}{N-r-1}+\frac{1-h}{N-r}.
\]

Thus
\[
\max \mathbb P(T=0)
=
1-N(1-p)\left(\frac{h}{N-r-1}+\frac{1-h}{N-r}\right),
\]
where
\[
h=(N-1)p(1-\rho)-r.
\]

Since \(T=0\) is exactly the event \(X_1=\cdots=X_N=1\), the largest possible value is

\[
\boxed{
1-N(1-p)\left(
\frac{(N-1)p(1-\rho)-r}{N-r-1}
+
\frac{1-(N-1)p(1-\rho)+r}{N-r}
\right)
}.
\]
